page: Google Cloud Platform n2d-highcpu-80 is an x86_64 compute instance powered by AMD EPYC 7B13 processors. The server provides 80 dedicated virtual CPUs derived from 40 physical cores with multithreading enabled, supported by 32 MB of L3 cache. Memory capacity is provisioned at 80.0 GB, yielding a 1:1 ratio of 1.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. The instance does not include integrated local disk storage, requiring external persistent disks, and operates without discrete GPU accelerators.

Benchmark results show competitive multi-threaded computational throughput. The instance achieves a top-tier score in PassMark CPU encryption benchmarks at 85,363.22, leveraging hardware acceleration features including AES, VAES, and SHA-NI extensions. In compute-intensive evaluations, the instance scored 107,952.86 in multi-core stress-ng tests and registered strong performance in Geekbench software compilation with Clang at 43,413.0, as well as ray tracing at 70,957.0. In-memory operations via Redis settled at 77.49 million operations per second.

The primary architectural constraint is the constrained memory footprint of 1.0 GB per vCPU and the absence of AVX-512 instruction support. While uncached read memory bandwidth runs within the median tier at 187.06 GB/sec, cached throughput reaches 5,077.68 GB/sec. This configuration offers high compute efficiency for CPU-bound tasks where per-thread memory footprint is minimal. It is well suited for distributed build clusters, batch compilation, continuous integration pipelines, video transcoding, and compute-focused microservices.
description: Google Cloud Platform n2d-highcpu-80 is a compute-focused instance based on the x86_64 AMD EPYC 7B13 processor family. It features 80 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 40 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading and 80.0 GB of system memory, establishing a 1.0 GB per vCPU allocation. The configuration contains no bundled local storage and no GPU accelerators. Benchmarks indicate high multi-threaded compute and encryption performance, evidenced by strong results in PassMark CPU encryption, Clang code compilation, and multi-core stress-ng assessments. Hardware crypto extensions such as AES, VAES, and SHA-NI accelerate cryptographic workflows, although the platform lacks AVX-512 extensions. The lean memory density positions the instance for high-throughput, compute-dominant workloads such as software compilation, batch processing pipelines, ray tracing, and compute-heavy containerized services.
